name: Stanz bei Landeck
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village above Landeck, home to Tirol’s oldest farmhouse and stunning views.
beschreibung:
Überblick

Stanz bei Landeck perches on a sun-drenched plateau at 1,040 metres above sea level on the southern slopes of the Lechtal Alps beneath the commanding Parseierspitze (3,036 m) in the Tyrolean district of Landeck. Rising two hundred metres above the valley basin of Landeck and Zams at the confluence of the Inn and Sanna rivers, this charming village is home to around 600 residents across some 150 households. Stanz enjoys international acclaim as Austria's first officially recognised distillery village ('Erstes Brennereidorf Österreichs') and an accredited culinary region. Blessed with an extraordinarily sunny microclimate exceeding 2,000 hours of sunshine annually, sweet fruit orchards flourish along the terraces, foremost among them the protected 'Stanzer Zwetschke' plum. With over 50 active private distilleries, Stanz boasts the highest distillery density in the world, captivating visitors with artisanal craft spirits, warm hospitality, and sweeping vistas over the Lechtal Alps and Upper Inntal.

Geschichte

Settlement on the Stanz plateau dates back to the Bronze Age, as evidenced by prehistoric discoveries and Roman coinage. The village was first documented in 1150 under the name 'Stanuc', pointing to pre-Roman origins denoting a stony slope or stream. The village's distilling lineage took root in the 18th century when Empress Maria Theresa granted royal distilling privileges to numerous local farms. Intense daytime sunshine coupled with crisp alpine nights creates an extraordinarily concentrated sugar content and aroma in the local plums, enabling Stanz distillers to achieve international renown. Furthermore, Stanz is the birthplace of one of the greatest architects of the European Baroque: Jakob Prandtauer was born here in 1660 at the Gasthof zum Löwen. Prandtauer rose to become Austria's premier master builder, immortalised by masterpieces such as the world-famous Melk Abbey along the Danube, Dürnstein Abbey, and Herzogenburg Abbey. Perched dramatically on a sheer rock pinnacle overlooking the Inn gorge stands the 12th-century Schrofenstein Castle ruin, a historic stronghold.

Anreise

By car, Stanz is accessed via the Inntal motorway A12 or the Arlberg expressway S16 to the Landeck/Zams interchange. From there, take the Reschenstraße B180 and the well-maintained Stanzer Landesstraße (L256), ascending to the sunny plateau in just five minutes (around four kilometres). Rail travellers arrive at the international railway hub of Landeck-Zams on the Arlberg line, where ÖBB Railjet, InterCity, and EuroCity trains call hourly. From the station forecourt, VVT regional bus route 4238 and local town bus line 6 run regularly to Stanz (stopping at Dorfplatz and Prandtauerweg). A scenic walking trail also connects Landeck to Stanz in approximately 45 minutes.

Tipps

A visit to Stanz centres on epicurean indulgence: almost every second household operates a distillery where guests can observe copper stills in action and taste award-winning brandies including plum, rowanberry, apple, and pear schnapps. The undisputed annual highlight is the culinary festival 'Stanz brennt', celebrated traditionally on the first Sunday of September, when dozens of farmsteads open their doors for live distilling demonstrations, live music, and regional specialties. Walkers should explore the themed Stanzer Zwetschke Trail, a gentle circuit winding through fruit orchards with informative displays. Culture seekers can admire the historic Prandtauer birthplace with its commemorative plaque and the parish church of Saints Peter and Paul. A walk out to the viewing platform beneath the Schrofenstein Castle ruins offers breathtaking panoramic views over Landeck Castle and the river valley below.
